Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Gwl:4279
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Gwalior
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajesh Kumar Gupta

On The 3 rd Of February, 2026
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 4746 of 2018
 Rohitashv
 Versus
 Yaswant Kumar
 Appearance:
 Shri Raj Kumar Singh Kushwaha - Advocate for the petiti
 Shri Nitin Sharma- Advocate for the respondent.
 Order

The instant petition has been filed under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. against the order dated 05.09.2017 passed in case No.70/2015 Criminal Revision by First Additional Sessions Judge, Sironj,
District vidisha, whereby by order passed by the JMFC, Sironj dated 17.04.2015 has been affirmed.

2. Brief facts of the case are that the petitioner had filed a complaint before the Judicial Court, upon which a charge-sheet was sought to be presented under Sections 406, 417 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code before t h e Judicial Magistrate First Class, Sironj, District Vidisha , against the respondent.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate First Class, Sironj, District Vidisha
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondent Yashwant Kumar Sharma is the owner of land bearing Survey Nos. 27 and 28, situated at Village Malsipur, Tehsil Sironj , having an area of 1.277 hectares and 0.063 hectares , respectively.

The respondent had developed a residential colony known as "Shivam Nagar NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4279 2 MCRC-4746-2018 Colony" on the said land during the years 1995-96, and sold plots therein to various persons, including the complainant.

entities.text: Shivam Nagar NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4279 2 MCRC-4746-2018 Colony
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The consideration amount of the plot purchased by the complainant/petitioner was payable in installments, and he had paid several installments towards the total consideration.
However, after collecting money from the purchasers, including the complainant, the accused Yashwant Kumar Sharma absconded from the city in the year 1995-96.
Thereafter, in the year 2013, the accused again started selling plots on the same land under a new colony name , thereby cheating innocent purchasers.
The accused has been selling the same plots repeatedly to different persons, thereby committing acts of cheating and criminal breach of trust.
In this regard, the complainant submitted a written complaint dated 23.07.2013 .

Prior thereto also, a complaint was made at Police Station Sironj seeking action against the accused; however, no action was taken by the police, compelling the complainant to file the present private complaint before the Court.

1 3.
In support of the complaint, the preliminary statements under Section 200 Cr.P.C. of the complainant and witnesses Mohammad Salman and Salauddin were recorded.
In his statement, the complainant categorically stated that he had purchased a plot in Shivam Nagar Colony during the years 1995-96 on an installment basis and had paid 20 installments .
He further stated that thereafter the accused absconded and, in the year 2013, again sold plots on the same land under the name of "Mahamai Kunj".
It was also stated that possession of the plot earlier sold to the complainant was never handed over to him.

Relevant documents and supporting evidence were also NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4279 3 MCRC-4746-2018 produced in support of the complaint and despite the aforesaid material on record, the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class,
Sironj , vide order dated 17.04.2015 , dismissed the complaint under Section 203 Cr.P.C. , holding that no sufficient ground existed to proceed.

Being aggrieved by the said order, the applicant preferred a Criminal Revision before the First Additional Sessions Judge, Sironj, District Vidisha ,
which was dismissed vide order dated 05.09.2017 .

entities.text: First Additional Sessions Judge, Sironj, District Vidisha
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Hence, being left with no other efficacious remedy, the applicant has preferred the present petition.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the learned Court below has dismissed the complaint of the complainant contrary to settled principles of law, and such dismissal is wholly unjustified.
The complainant examined himself as a witness in support of his complaint and also examined two other witnesses, namely Mohammad Salman and Salauddin , whose statements were duly recorded.

From the said evidence, it stood well established that the respondent is the owner of land bearing Survey No. 27 admeasuring 1.277 hectares and Survey No. 28 admeasuring 0.063 hectares, situated at Village Malsipur, Tehsil Sironj , and that the respondent had developed Shivam Nagar Colony on the said land during the years 1995-96 and sold plots to various residents of Sironj town.
The complainant had also purchased a plot from the respondent, and several other persons had similarly purchased plots from him.
The complainant had paid installments towards the consideration amount and produced receipts issued from the office of the respondent along with the complaint.
Thereafter, the respondent absconded from Sironj.
Relevant documents were also produced.

The complainant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4279 4 MCRC-4746-2018 further produced the Patwari report and site panchnama, which clearly established that the land in question was diverted for residential purposes.
Thus, prima facie material was available to establish the commission of offences under Sections 420, 406 and 417 IPC against the respondent.
Despite this, the learned subordinate court committed a grave judicial error in dismissing the complaint.

5. The learned Court below dismissed the complaint on the ground that the receipts produced did not bear the signatures of the respondent and that the publicity pamphlet of Shivam Nagar Colony did not mention the survey numbers or the name of the seller.
The said reasoning is erroneous and unsustainable in law.
It is a matter of common experience that a person intending to cheat often adopts such methods in advance to conceal his identity, as has been done by the non-applicant in the present case.

Mere absence of survey numbers or the name of the seller on a pamphlet cannot be a valid ground for dismissal of the complaint, particularly when sufficient oral and documentary evidence exists on record to prima facie establish the commission of offences by the respondent.

Rohitashv vs Yaswant Kumar on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87871099/
2 6.

The learned Court below further committed a serious judicial error by dismissing the complaint on the ground that the complainant failed to prove that Mahamai Kunj Colony was being developed and sold by the respondent-Yashwant Kumar Sharma , and that the complainant did not produce any document relating to colonizer license or permission from the Municipal Corporation.
The said approach is completely misconceived and contrary to law.
The burden of producing such documents does not lie upon NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4279 5 MCRC-4746-2018 the complainant.
Acceptance of such reasoning would lead to an absurd situation where a person cheating without obtaining any licence would be treated as innocent, while only a licensed coloniser could be prosecuted.
The analysis and conclusion drawn by the learned Court below are therefore patently illegal and unsustainable.

At the stage of taking cognizance and registration of a complaint,
the Court is only required to see whether the essential ingredients of the alleged offences are prima facie made out from the complaint and the evidence produced in support thereof.
It is not necessary for the complainant to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt or establish evidence sufficient for conviction at that stage.
The impugned order passed by the learned subordinate court, being contrary to the settled position of law, is therefore liable to be quashed.
7. Learned counsel for the respondent opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection by supporting the impugned orders.
He further submitted that there is material contradictions in the complaint filed by the petitioner.

8. Heard counsel for the rival parties and perused the entire record with due care.
9.
From perusal of the record, this court finds that there are concurrent findings recorded by both the courts below.

It is also evident that the name of the respondent is not mentioned in the plot for which sale advertisement was issued in the name of Mahamai Kunj and there is no mention of the Khasra number of the said land in it.

10 It is also noteworthy here that on behalf of the complainant, no document of the colonizer license of the respondent and permission of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4279 6 MCRC-4746-2018 Directorate of Town and Country Planning has been presented in the courts below.
11. However, learned counsel for the petitioner has produced certain documents before this court in support of his submissions to prove his case.
But, the aforesaid documents have not been produced following the due procedure through Registry of this Court.
Therefore, the aforesaid documents cannot be relied upon by this court to go into the merits of the case.

12. However, in the interest of justice, both the orders passed by the courts below (order dated 05.09.2018 passed by the Sessions Court and order dated 17.04.2015 passed by JMFC) are hereby set aside and the matter is remanded to the trial court with a direction to the trial court that if the petitioner produces certain documents as per law in support of his contention, then trial court is directed to take the aforesaid documents on record in accordance with law and while appreciating the validity of the aforesaid documents in proper manner, shall decide the case afresh.

Rohitashv vs Yaswant Kumar on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87871099/
3 13.
With the aforesaid direction, this petition is disposed of.

(RAJESH KUMAR GUPTA ) JUDGE Vishal Rohitashv vs Yaswant Kumar on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87871099/
